chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah from his father (a.s.) who said:
It was mentioned in the will of Amir al-Mumineen (a.s.) who said: Do not leave the Hajj of the House of your Lord else you will be destroyed.

And he said: One who does not perform the Hajj because of a need from the needs of the world, his need will not be fulfilled until he looks at the shavers (the pilgrims returning after completing the Hajj rituals).

key_terms.الْمُحَلِّقِینَ: The shavers (referring to pilgrims completing Hajj rituals)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of leaving Hajj for worldly needs according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam Ali’s will in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this narration underscores Hajj as a critical pillar whose neglect invites spiritual ruin. It establishes a causal link between prioritizing worldly affairs over the pilgrimage and the postponement of their resolution, specifically noting that one must wait to see the returning pilgrims (*al-muḥalliqīn*) before their needs are met. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Hajj as both a physical duty and a transformative spiritual event that influences worldly outcomes.
